procedure: Preserve the unchanged customer request outside the business blueprint.
Use the selected task skill and compiled ora_rule_registry.json to resolve task semantics and blockers.

Write only explicit operations, target keys, requested values, resolved scope, defaults, prerequisites, preservation assertions, and warnings into the normalized design input. For a requested one-year Generate Periods action, set generatePeriods=true on the AP_OTHER_PERIOD_TYPE create operation; supply source codes for PeriodFrequency and PeriodNameFormat, the matching PeriodsPerYear, and StartDate. Do not also supply manual child periods for that calendar. OTHER requires manually defined child rows.

Apply this workflow to any supported calendar setup, update, migration, or test request. Use the actual source context; do not assume EBS. Run normalize to emit the validated blueprint, disclosed preview and stable requirements list.

Only for a user-confirmed EBS source, set resolvedScope.sourceSystem=EBS and apply the EBS period-name review before candidate generation: present source PeriodName versus EnteredPeriodName plus two-digit PeriodYear. Require exact per-row periodNameDecisions for changes; acceptance preserves sourcePeriodName metadata and uses the predicted target key. Generic package approval does not imply rename consent.

EffectiveFrom.boundary: Optional on create; preserve an omitted or blank value without defaulting it from StartDate. GENERAL FSM import and fresh-export readback verified blank persistence; PAYMENT TERMS omission has not been live-tested. Validate supplied date ordering. FSM service field is insert-only (while_insert); changing or clearing EffectiveFrom on an existing calendar through FSM is unsupported. Preserve its baseline value during other updates.

StartDate.boundary: Generation setting, not universally required: for PeriodFrequency OTHER leave blank and do not derive from child periods. A populated OTHER header StartDate is rejected before candidate creation rather than silently discarded. Generation frequencies require their start date; period-row dates remain independently required.
